title: Triangle shawl with shell border
subtitle: A top-down triangle in half treble, finished with a shell-stitch border in DK cotton
excerpt: This top-down triangular shawl grows from a chain-2 spine into a full triangle in half treble, then gains a shell-stitch border along the lower two edges. Finished size is roughly 145 cm wide and 70 cm deep in DK cotton on a 4.5 mm hook. The half treble body gives a dense, warm fabric; the shell border adds decorative width.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 2 (1886), triangular shawl construction from a centre-chain spine (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet shawl chapter.
heroPrompt: A triangular crochet shawl in ivory DK cotton draped over a wooden chair back, photographed from the side in soft natural light, the shell border is clearly visible along both diagonal edges.

glossaryTerms.definition: The central vertical chain that divides a top-down triangular shawl into two equal halves. Increases work on either side of the spine each row.
A decorative border worked by making five trebles into one stitch or space, creating fan shapes along the edge.

content.text: This triangular shawl grows from a two-chain spine at the neck down to a full-width point, worked in half treble on a 4.5 mm hook with DK cotton. The body fabric is dense enough to drape without stretching out of shape. The shell-stitch border runs along both diagonal edges and turns the corners cleanly.
The construction is top-down: you start at the top centre with a short chain, place a stitch marker on the centre chain (the
spine
), and increase by one half treble on each side of it on every row. The shawl is 70 rows deep before the border.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 400 g DK-weight cotton yarn. A 4.5 mm crochet hook (US 7). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Stitch marker. Blocking mat and pins. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

16 htr × 12 rows = 10 × 10 cm in DK cotton with a 4.5 mm hook, measured unstretched. Work a 15 × 15 cm swatch in half treble, measure the central 10 × 10 cm area, and swap hook size if the tension misses by more than one stitch per 10 cm. The gauge (older British patterns call this a tension square) controls the finished width.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
half treble (htr): UK; the same move as US "half double crochet" (hdc).
treble (tr): UK; the same move as US "double crochet" (dc).
Pattern
The shawl is worked flat, turning at the end of each row. The spine sits at the centre of every row; mark it with a stitch marker that you move up each row.
Foundation
Ch 4. Place a stitch marker in the 2nd ch from the hook, this is the spine chain.
Row 1 (right side)

Ch 2 (does not count as a stitch). 1 htr in each of the 2 foundation chains before the spine. Move marker to the spine ch. 1 htr in the spine ch. 1 htr in each of the remaining 2 foundation chains. Turn. (5 sts)
Row 2 (wrong side)

Ch 2 (does not count as a stitch). 1 htr in each st to 1 st before the spine st. 2 htr in the st before the spine. 1 htr in the spine st (move marker). 2 htr in the st after the spine. 1 htr in each st to end. Turn. (7 sts)
Rows 3 to 70

Repeat Row 2 on every row. On every row, two stitches increase (one on each side of the spine). At the end of Row 70 you have 145 sts. Move the marker up the spine on each row to keep track of the centre.
Shell border
Work the
shell border
along both diagonal edges of the shawl. Do not work along the straight top edge.

Starting at the top right corner: join yarn. *Sk 2 sts (or 2 row-ends), 5 tr in the next st (or row-end), sk 2 sts (or row-ends), 1 sl st in the next st (or row-end)*; repeat from * to * along the right diagonal edge to the bottom point. At the bottom point, work (5 tr, ch 2, 5 tr) into the single bottom stitch to turn the corner. Continue the shell repeat up the left diagonal edge to the top left corner. Fasten off.
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in all ends through the backs of several stitches in different directions. To wet-block, soak the shawl in cool water for 10 minutes. Gently press out excess water in a towel. Pin the shawl to a blocking mat at the finished dimensions. Leave until completely dry.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap. Do not tumble-dry. Lay flat on a clean towel and ease to shape while damp.
What to try next

Work the same construction in lace-weight yarn on a 3 mm hook for a finer, more open fabric. Swap the half treble body for treble stitch throughout to add height and drape. A contrast colour for the shell border gives a clean two-tone finish.
